newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul won ends higher in line with yen's strength.
newsitem.headline: Seoul won ends higher in line with yen's strength.

text.p: The won closed firmer against the dollar on Wednesday in line with the yen's strength versus the dollar in global markets, dealers said.
But fears of the Bank of Korea's dollar buying intervention limited the won's rise, they said.
The won closed at 890.40, compared with Tuesday's closing of 891.10. It opened at a low of 890.90 and hit a high of 890.10.
"The yen's rise was a main factor. But traders were also mindful of the central bank's possible intervention," said a foreign bank dealer.
The yen fell to 110.78/88 in Tokyo market on Wednesday from 12.98/13.00 on Tuesday.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 890.60 on Thursday, compared with 891.10 today.
Dealers said the central bank seemed to want the dollar at above 890 level in the hopes that the high dollar would help improve South Korea's trade balance.
The foreign bank dealer forecast trading would range from 889.50 to 891.50 on Thursday, while a domestic bank dealer put it between 889.00 and 891.00.
